reasons: Lake identity record confirms United States v. Lewis / United States v. Edward Leonidas Lewis, Sixth Circuit, decided 2023-09-01, docket 22-5593.
Lake citations record marks the case slip-only with no official reporter citation, consistent with the page's slip-style citation.
residual_risks: Opinion caption also lists Nos. 22-5593/5800, while the lake docket field and page cite use 22-5593.

defect.evidence_quote: During [the] search it became apparent that Mr. Lewis had used his laptop to view images of child sexual exploitation.
defect.locator_note: text/United States v. Lewis__488b0b.txt, quoted affidavit in probable-cause section
defect.problem: The holding is substantively supported, but the quoted fragment 'become apparent' is not character-faithful to the disclosed opinion/affidavit language, which says 'it became apparent.'
defect.proposed_fix: Change the fragment to quote the exact language: the affidavit stated that during the search 'it became apparent' Lewis had used his laptop to view images of child sexual exploitation, or remove quotation marks from the paraphrase.

reasons: The opinion holds Lewis consented to the initial laptop and phone search but not the later seizure or forensic examination.
The opinion holds the affidavit failed probable cause because it supplied only conclusory assertions without facts a magistrate could independently evaluate.
The opinion holds the affidavit was bare bones and the good-faith exception was inapplicable.
residual_risks: The word 'homeowner' is slightly stronger than the disclosed evidence, which confirms Lewis's home/residence but does not separately prove ownership.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use 'resident' or 'defendant' instead of 'homeowner' if ownership precision matters.

reasons: Consent scope is a substantial part of the opinion: the court held Lewis consented to the initial on-site search but not to seizure or later forensic examination.
The conclusion expressly distinguishes admissible evidence from the initial consent search from evidence obtained through unsupported later searches and seizures.
residual_risks: No disclosed corpus rubric defines when a case is 'Key,' but the consent-search holding is central enough to support that role.

reasons: Treatment/currency is outside Lens A, but the disclosed text identifies a recommended-for-publication Sixth Circuit opinion.
Lake identity confirms court_level coa and circuit ca6, supporting the in-circuit weight label.
residual_risks: No Lens A treatment finding made.

reasons: Treatment/currency is outside Lens A, and the content treatment fields match the lake record's unverified treatment fields.
Lake treatment records field_i_validity and composite_basis as unverified, null as-of fields, varies_by_point false, and the same frontier-stub scope note.
residual_risks: No Lens A treatment finding made.
